name: Epiphyte
desc: Epiphytes colonising the boughs of a host tree in humid gloom — windborne plumed propagules land on bare bark and each site walks the whole successional sequence from pioneer crust to moss cushion to strap-leaved bromeliad rosette to orchid with pseudobulbs and an arching flower spike, aerial roots dangling and swaying beneath, until the mature growth lets go and drops and the freed bark is colonised again.

energy.doc: breeze through the boughs — root sway, leaf flutter, spike whip — plus succession rate

density.doc: how many colonised sites are rendered (3 at 0 -> 16 at 1) and how thick the propagule rain is

scale.doc: epiphyte size vs frame (2.2 = a macro study of a few plants)

hue.doc: foliage hue (flowers always sit opposite it, senescence drifts it warm)

boughs.doc: how many host branches, each on its own depth plane

x.doc: colonisation focus — where the propagule rain converges, and therefore where new sites establish along the boughs

y.doc: height of the bough stack in the frame

style.doc: aesthetic — dense botanical wash w/ bark fissures and top-light; Atkins photogram on Prussian blue; additive translucent radiograph; nocturne where form is built only from a drifting canopy dapple

seed.doc: seeds the boughs, colonisation sites, plant proportions and root counts

alpha.doc: opacity of the epiphytes over the boughs
